dedupe_keys.name: building loss and rebuilding within wildfire perimeters of the conterminous us 2000 to 2013

description: This Forest Service data publication maps what happened to buildings inside wildfire perimeters in the wildland-urban interface (WUI), showing which buildings were destroyed and whether they were rebuilt or joined by new construction afterwards. It covers wildfires that destroyed buildings in the conterminous United States between 2000 and 2013, with building destruction, rebuilding and new construction shown as points, and older fires followed over a longer time since fire. It was produced by H. Anu Kramer, Miranda Mockrin, Patricia Alexandre, Susan Stewart and Volker Radeloff, funded by the Joint Fire Science Program, and published in the Forest Service Research Data Archive in 2023 as RDS-2023-0040. It is available for download as tabular data and vector point data; no licence is named, but the archive states the data were collected with US Government funding and can be used without additional permissions or fees, with citation, so they are free. Caveats: it records only fires that destroyed buildings in that period and does not include recent fires. It supports wildfire exposure and recovery analysis for buildings at the interface between vegetation and settlements, including rebuilding rates for resilience models; a related record is the State of Wildfires exposure datasets.
